description: "The Death of Balder" by Johannes Ewald is a tragedy written in the late 18th century, rooted in Danish folklore and mythology. This work explores the complexities of love, honor, and fate through its central characters: Balder, the half-god son of Odin, and Hother, a mortal prince who finds himself ensnared in a web of tragic circumstances and rivalries over the affections of Nanna, the daughter of Gevar.
